Motivation¶

Front month futures contracts dominate futures trading volume. Leading up to a particular front month expiry, many thus 'roll' their position over to the next front month contract. This process can lead to mispricings around the roll. A mean reversion algorithm was thus applied to the calendar price spread between front two month futures contracts of various index and commodity futures in this volatile period. The algorithm bets that deviations from long established calendar price spreads are more likely to be mispricings resulting from roll volatility than legitimate price discovery. Brent oil futures are used here as an example.

Backtest Data¶

2 years of 5 secondly, brent oil futures data was collected from Refinitiv Datascope. Given that there are monthly expiries of this contract, the strategy was tested on dozens of front month roll periods. Specifically, the mean reversion algorithm was only applied on exact expiry days where volatility is most noticeable. Below, the data is explored, cleaned and then examples of calendar price spreads between front 2 month contracts (and their mean reverting behaviour) on these days are plotted.

    unique_hours_per_day[day] = unique_hours

Strategy¶

Below, a custom mean reversion algorithm is applied on each front month expiry day. It essentially trades the spread (either long front month and short second front month or vice versa) on 0.15 index point deviations from the previous mean. PnL graphs and total index point profit is displayed

In [ ]:
from python_trading_functions import mean_reversion_algorithm

running_totals = []
for considered in range(len(dfels)):
    dfe = dfels[considered][0]
    dfl = dfels[considered][1]
    start_closing = close_times[considered]

    result_df = pd.DataFrame(columns=['date', 'theo_spread', 'theo_value1', 'theo_value2', 'open_positions', 'amounte', 'amountl', 'cash', 'to_close_spread', 'cumulative', 'slippage'])

    rows = mean_reversion_algorithm(0.15, 1, start_closing)
    result_df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=result_df.columns)

    if result_df.shape[0] > 0:
        final_pnl = list(result_df['cumulative'])[-1]

        print(final_pnl)
        running_totals.append(final_pnl)

        result_df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(result_df['date'])
        result_df.sort_values(by='date', inplace=True)
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
        plt.plot(pd.to_datetime(result_df['date'])[::40], result_df['cumulative'][::40], label='PnL')
        plt.xlabel('Date')
        plt.ylabel('cumulative')
        plt.title('cumulative Over Time')
        plt.xticks(rotation=45)
        plt.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

Results¶

On average, the strategy makes 0.4 index points per front month expiry day of trading. This represents a roughly 1% ROI per day of investment which is significant. However, only 12 such days per year would be tradeable for Brent and there is low volume at the proposed trade points. Furthermore, retails investors aren't allowed to trade most commodity futures this close to expiry given that they can't guarantee physical delviery. An interactive brokers trading bot was set up to paper trade this algorithm.
